jdpuzd2zog We reason "at the margin" because your decision is made unit by unit: buy the 11th panel or not. What counts is what THIS panel adds (§2.1).

2byyf7bcxvx This is demand: if the price is p, you keep buying as long as the next panel is worth at least p to you. At each price, the quantity bought is where MPB = p. The MPB curve IS demand, in inverse form (§2.4).

9aybpj647k The manufacturer asks the mirror question: "how much does ONE more panel cost me?" The first ones come off the most efficient machines; to make more, you need overtime and pricier materials. The cost of the next panel rises.
14rcw142akq Under competition, supply is the [[MPC]] curve: the firm produces as long as p ≥ MC (§6.5). In A6: {{MPC = 10 + 2Q}}.
5jcbep17y6 The curve slopes up: producing more forces the use of ever more costly resources, so the cost of the NEXT unit rises (§6.4).
25g2u8o5cxy This is supply: a price-taking firm produces as long as the price covers the cost of the next panel, and stops where p = MC (§6.5). At each price, the quantity supplied is read off MPC.
8lnk55kvx3 "Private" because it is the cost THE PRODUCER pays. If its factory imposed a cost on others (noise, smoke), that would not be in it. Here, we assume there is none.

27nob5dxz5z As long as a panel is worth more to the buyer than it costs the manufacturer, there is a price that suits both: it gets sold. At the 18th panel, value = cost = €46. The 19th is worth €43 to the buyer but costs €48 to make: no price suits both. Trade stops at 18.

1jk1mof20ae Which equality describes this stopping point?

i1nd8dch8w At the 19th: 43 < 48. For the manufacturer to accept, the price must be ≥ 48; for the buyer to accept, ≤ 43. No price satisfies both.
1vgb3mjjnye At p = 46, the quantity buyers want (18) equals the quantity sellers want (18): nobody gains by changing. That is the equilibrium (§3, F01).
ptaal04a5z At the Saturday market, each panel sold is a handshake. The 19th: the seller says "48 minimum", the buyer "43 maximum". No handshake.

1yfgeb9mrg2 What is this effect called?

1tgna2kjwu9 An effect on third parties that is not taken into account in the transaction is called an **externality**. When the effect is good for third parties, it is a **positive externality**. A factory's pollution would be a negative externality.
1vuf5a1dch3 Externality: an effect on a third party, not taken into account in the transaction (§11.1). Positive: vaccination, research, networks. Negative: pollution, noise.
27ps17dwkn1 "External" because the effect leaves the buyer–seller circle: it reaches someone outside.

16v07gqmihw An effect that goes THROUGH a price is not one: if the price of milk rises and makes your coffee pricier, you pay and someone receives. An externality is precisely an effect that has NO price.
29ffz7ty3ik It matters because the market only adds up what has a price. What has none is ignored in the decision — hence a quantity that can be bad for society.
xejvsd5ang Positive: vaccination, shared research, beehives next to an orchard. Negative: pollution, noise (E2025 Q1c), a coal plant (E2021 Q1c).
1kopch8p8x4 Your action (buying panels) has a consequence (cleaner air) for people who are not in your transaction. That's it — that is an externality.
hf2slb3l0x Still nothing new on the graph: naming the effect does not bring it into prices.

1m22t4ygb25 Yes: a benefit for third parties, without payment.
1zhzkcj5hf8 Your coffee costs more because the price of milk went up

13vs9x5fz3s We measure the externality like everything else: for ONE more panel. The benefit an extra panel creates for others is called the [[MEB]]. Here, each extra panel brings €20 to the neighbours, whatever the number already installed.
23d7zrmc5di [[MEB]] = 20, constant: each extra unit gives third parties a benefit of 20. The TOTAL external benefit of Q units is the area under MEB (20Q).
1dllfxsmihv We measure "per panel" because all decisions are made at the margin. The externality must be in the same unit (€ per panel) so it can be added to the other values.
112kaf750g0 Constant here by assumption of exercise A6: each panel replaces the same amount of pollution. It is not a law — MEB can depend on Q (last block).
2b66na2hcx2 MEB is a MARGINAL, not a total: the TOTAL external benefit of 18 panels is 18 × 20 = 360, the area under MEB (§11.1).
1055ecdzc0o If each panel avoided 0.1 tonne of CO₂ valued at €200 per tonne, we would get MEB = €20 per panel (illustrative figures).
6stqd0bm3h Each time you screw in a panel, picture €20 dropping into your neighbours' (invisible) pocket — not yours.
1ft9w5rd5dj The purple line MEB = 20: it is not a market curve (nobody buys it). It is the value, for third parties, of each extra panel.
fv6i6jikup receive MEB = €20
1jrhlxbx5jn At the 18th panel, how much does the WHOLE of society (you + your neighbours) gain from this panel?
11j42fgi5pn Your share: MPB(18). The neighbours' share: MEB.
1tx6m7eki80 MPB(18) + MEB = 46 + 20 = €66. You have just computed one point of the future MSB curve.
1bhxbruv27p 20 is only the neighbours' share (MEB). Add yours.

1i2xgzo6fnk Nobody "pays out" MSB. It is a measure of VALUE: what the panel is worth to everyone together. The state may later spend money (a subsidy), but MSB exists even if it does nothing.
1c0gm6awwxu We add because society is everyone. If a panel is worth 46 to one person and 20 to the others, it is worth 66 to all together: the values of different people for the SAME unit add up.
25eyrf7rd4t We add vertically, at the same Q, because it is the SAME panel that benefits the buyer and the neighbours — exactly as for a public good (§11.8).
o753nfz3g5 MSB lies above MPB because MEB > 0: each unit has value on top of what the buyer sees.
